```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

tweets <- read_csv("data/tweets.csv")

```

## The Data
This data was taken from the Barack Obama Presidential Library created by the National Archives. The data set contains information about every Tweet made by Obama through the @POTUS44 handle. 

You can access the data for yourself here: [National Archives - Obama Tweets](https://www.obamalibrary.gov/digital-research-room/archived-white-house-websites-and-social-media)

```{r}
glimpse(tweets)
```

DATA Cleaning
```{r}
tweets2 <- tweets |> 
    mutate(
        timestamp = ymd_hms(timestamp),
        text_lower = str_to_lower(text),
        text = str_replace_all(text, "&amp;", "&")
    )
```

## Text Analysis

#### Tweet Length
```{r}
tweets1 <- tweets2 |> 
    filter(!is.na(text)) |> 
    mutate(length = str_length(text_lower)) |> 
    mutate(mean = mean(length)) |> 
    mutate(length_ratio = length/mean) |> 
    select(length_ratio, length, tweet_id, timestamp, text, source) |> 
    arrange(desc(length))
tweets1 |> 
    summarize(mean = mean(length), max = max(length), min = min(length))
```

The mean length of the Tweets is 128 characters. This table displays the length of each post in descending order. Further, it takes the relative length of each post to the mean. The longest post had 171 characters, and the shortest Tweet contained only 17 characters. 

```{r}
tweets1 |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=timestamp, y=length)) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.15,size=0.8, color = "steelblue") +
    labs(title = "Length of Obama's Tweets Over Time", 
            x = "Date Posted", y = "Tweet Length (characters)") +
    theme_void()
```

#### tweets per month/ per year
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    mutate(month = month(timestamp)) |> 
    group_by(month) |> 
    summarize(n=n())
```


```{r}
ggplot(__, aes(x = month)) +
    geom_bar() + 
    labs(title = "Obama's Tweets by Month", x = "", y = "")
```
